q1.question: How difficult is the ride?
q1.answer: This tour is suitable for casual and occasional cyclists, requiring moderate fitness and cycling ability. Out of the 4 hours of each tour, roughly 90 minutes will be on the bikes, with the rest on foot exploring the locations. The cycling is done in 10~15 minute chunks, or as needed to accommodate everyone and ensure a safe and comfortable experience. Crucially, the electric assist of the bikes make the uphill sections manageable even for casual cyclists.

q2.question: Do you cycle on roads or footpaths?
q2.answer: We cycle exclusively on roads shared with cars. This is because the roads provide the best cycling experience and views, but also because cycling is not permitted in Minoh Park. The roads we take are either marked with "Cycle Friendly" signs, or lesser-traveled mountain roads. That said, it is important to cycle responsibly and be mindful of cars, and follow the instructions of the guide in order to stay safe.

q3.question: Are tours cancelled in the case of bad weather?
q3.answer: In the case of heavy rain or other dangerous conditions, tours will be canceled and fully refunded on the day of travel, at the discretion of Minoh Cycles.

q4.question: How far is the ride?
q4.answer: Tours cover a distance of 16 kilometers - It's an 8 kilometer ride from the meeting point to Katsuoji, and we follow the same route back.

q5.question: What ages is this tour suitable for?
q5.answer: So far, we've had teenagers, up to people in their sixties come and enjoy this tour, although all the older guests have also been keen cyclists.

q6.question: How much traffic is there on the roads?
q6.answer: The route is on quiet public roads, with a speed limit of 30km/hour. There is usually at least some cars, but this can increase during the autumn leaves period (mid November-early December) when the area is most popular.

q7.question: Do I need to bring my own water?
q7.answer: A 500ml bottle of water will be provided, but in the warmer months you are strongly encouraged to bring more or money to buy more at the vending machines at Katsuoji and the falls.

q9.question: Can I leave a bag for safe keeping?
q9.answer: Yes, you can leave luggage at the meeting point, which will be locked during the ride.

q10.question: Do I need insurance?
q10.answer: While riding, you will be insured under the TS Mark system. This pays out compensation in the case of injuries to yourself, and liability to third parties that are involved in any accidents. For details please refer to {link}.

q11.question: How large is each tour group?
q11.answer: Tours are currently offered to groups of up to 5 people at once. This relatively small size ensures the guide can keep everyone together safely on the roads, and an intimate personalized experience where everyone can ask as many questions as they like.

q12.question: Who is this tour NOT suitable for?
q12.answer: This tour is not recommended for the following groups:
items: Serious cyclists looking for a more challenging, extended ride. Since we use e-bikes, the hill climbs are frankly not particularly challenging. Furthermore, in order to enjoy the scenery and accommodate less experienced cyclists, we tend to go at a leisurely pace. For a sportier road-bike experience, we recommend you check out Road Bike Rental Japan (RBRJ).

People not confident cycling on the road with cars. Whilst the roads we will use are not particularly busy, and have low speed limits, we cannot recommend our tours to anyone for whom that will be big issue.

Those looking to walk the trail from Minoh Station up to the waterfall (Minoh Park). Whether that's because you would prefer to walk through the forest, or you specifically want to see the Minoh Park Insect Museum and Ryuanji Temple, our tour does not go along the main Minoh Park trail. If you want to see everything Minoh has to offer and also have an afternoon free though, we recommend taking our tour in the morning, then walking up to Ryuanji temple in the afternoon.
